question.text: The checklist-based approach to research reports recommended in Chapter 13 helps ensure:

answer.text: Reports are as short as possible
Consistency, completeness, and quality across all research outputs
Reports are only for institutional investors

explanation.text: The Logic: The checklist approach supports consistency in decision making, discipline, the avoidance of mistakes or shortcuts, objective fact-based decisions and a clear decision trail. The sample checklists cover qualitative, quantitative and valuation items used to build the research view. The Trap: Checklists are not aimed at brevity. They apply to all report types and audiences and structure the substantive analysis rather than the formatting or length. Note: The sample checklist pages do not extend to disclosures and disclaimers; keep those as a separate compliance layer addressed under the regulatory chapters.
